They share the substantive gravitation concept space — freefall under gravity and the inverse-square universal law of gravitation are mutually reinforcing facets of the same chapter — so there is genuine conceptual coherence beyond the shared parent chapter. However, neither is evidenced as supporting success in the other: explaining freefall does not require the historical narrative, and the poster-based historical description does not depend on freefall proficiency; with equal Class IX rank and no substantive asymmetry evidence, a developmental direction is not warranted. Remaining nomination signals (shared ancestors, page-43 proximity, stopword-level token overlap) are non-semantic. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context, which limits but does not contradict this symmetric reading.
